title: Airbrush ribbon

reference.source: Reference 10: 1980s airbrush illustration on black, 1000 × 675 px
reference.note: held locally; this page carries statistics measured from it and none of its pixels

summary: A translucent band coiled on one axis: its color is a ramp over the surface normal, its layers stack like gels, thin helices add their glow with a depth test, and one airbrush bloom sits over a 39 px floor grid.
units: reference pixels; the plate is 1000 × 675 and every length scales with the canvas

turns.does: How many times the band goes around the axis. 1.85 ends the band at the front, just under the sphere line.

radius.does: Radius of the coil. The reference loop spans 600 px of a 675 px sheet.

band.does: Width of the strip along the axis. The reference band is 200 px wide at the loop.

pitch.does: Axial advance per turn at the start. Below the band width the far side shows through the near side.

open.does: Cubic growth of the pitch along the coil: a tight loop that opens into the long sweep.

start.does: Where on the circle the band begins. 2.6 rad hides the start at the lower front.

shift.does: Slides the whole coil along its axis.

persp.does: Near parts of the coil drawn larger. At .4 the near face is 12 % wider than the far face.

opacity.does: Share of the near layer in the mix. At .84 the far side reads through at 16 %.

tint.does: How much a layer tints what lies behind it and darkens a layer stacked on it.

lamp.does: The key light sits at the right. The band at the left edge is dimmed by this fraction.

streak.does: Passes of the gun along the band, read as faint 34 px streaks.

edge.does: Softness of the frisket edge. The reference edge turns over in 1.5 px.

rimGlow.does: Blue light from the floor on the band's cut end and on down-facing parts.

arcs.does: Count of thin additive helices on the same axis.

arcCore.does: Sigma of the bright core of each helix.

arcGlow.does: Sigma of the sprayed skirt around the core. A second skirt sits at 5 times this radius.

arcGain.does: Brightness of the helices. At 1 the yellow core peaks at the measured 228, 181, 89.

spheres.does: Count of lit balls along the axis, spaced 78 px apart.

halo.does: Overspray around each masked ball, a 6 px blur that lifts the black beside it.

sphereR.does: Radius of each ball. Measured 18 px.

gridPitch.does: Spacing of the floor grid at the bottom edge. Measured 39 px.

gridGlow.does: Brightness of the grid lines and their 2.2 px glow. 0 removes the floor.

horizon.does: Vanishing height of the floor. The band's axis sits 8 px above it.

haze.does: Blue light lifting the black toward the foot, and the 9 px glow around the grid.

bloom.does: Radius of the haze that every light throws past its own edge.

bloomGain.does: How much of that haze is added back.

grain.does: Noise of the printed, scanned original: a 0.75 px blurred field plus a 30 px mottle. Measured σ 2.6 on the black.

seed.does: Re-rolls sphere colors and helix placement.

phase.does: Position along the loop. The coil turns once about the axis per unit; the light helices turn one and a half times.

modes.saw: value up to value + amp over period seconds, then again
modes.drift: seeded walk, one step of up to amp every period seconds, folded back at the slider ends

motion.runs: only while Motion is on, at half scale; the sliders hold the center values; off by default

live.runs: only while Live is on: a drag on the figure sets x across and y down between these ends; off by default

techniques.name: Pull
techniques.implementation: Single-layer face: the ramp from the top glint through the dark fold to [254,71,24]

techniques.name: Glow
techniques.implementation: Light helix: a σ 1.3 px core over a σ 3.8 px skirt, added over black

techniques.name: Edge
techniques.implementation: Frisket edge: the band turns over in 1.3 px, then the glint starts

techniques.name: Grain
techniques.implementation: Floor grid, 39 px at the foot, rows closing as (y − horizon)²

pass_order: base: black, a blue haze from the horizon down, the floor grid drawn once at 1.5 px and glowed at 2.2 px and 9 px
spheres on the axis at depth zero: lambert discs lit from the right, a hard 1 px mask edge, a 6 px overspray halo
light helices on the same axis: gaussian cores splatted with a wide depth kernel, then a 3.8 px skirt and a 19 px skirt per channel

the band: sliced by rows into spans that carry depth and normal angle; per pixel the spans composite far to near as gels (opacity, tint, stacking), with the spheres and the helices inserted at their depth
cut end of the band: a 3 px and a 13 px blue edge light
one 7 px bloom at 4 %, then scan grain scaled 1.45× on the band

measured.ribbon_single_layer_ramp: x=760 column: top glint [236,109,58], dark fold [168,73,53] at θ≈.5, saturated [254,71,24] at θ .8 to 1.3, pink [198,134,88] and blue [90,136,221] at the cut end
measured.ribbon_double_layer: x=230 column: [175 to 197,80,50] where the loop's back shows through the front, [115,65,48] in the darkest overlap
measured.back_face: [37,27,31] at x 600 to 660, the band seen from behind
measured.sphere_shade: L 47 at the left edge to 179 five px right of center, no specular
measured.grid_row_spacing_px: 7 at y 585 to 12 at y 656, proportional to (y − 350)²
measured.rejected: a Lambert shade over the normal: the measured ramp has a dark fold at θ .5 between two bright zones, which no single light direction gives

benchmark.computed: live, when this page loads, by the code that measured the reference: default parameters, Hot orange palette, 1× reference size

setup.note: Composition is generated; the ribbon face, arc, sphere and grid patches were placed with search.py on the default render and then fixed by hand to the equivalent material events.

limits: Benchmark 95.4 % mean. The sphere-row histogram (86 %) and the whole-plate histogram (90 %) miss because the reference spheres are shaded by hand with a flatter yellow and a steeper green, and the reference's left loop carries a yellow glint from an arc behind it that the generated coil does not reproduce.
The ribbon-face patch includes the band seen from behind; the reference's back face is [37,27,31] gray, the rebuild's is [47,27,22], so the dark ink color scores 91 %.
The coil, helices and sphere colors are generated; whole-plate ink shares are matched by the coil's scale, not by position.
The reference is a JPEG scan; its ringing around the arcs is not reproduced.
notes: Deterministic: the same palette, parameters and seed give the same pixels.
A display render is capped at 2.4 megapixels; a slider in motion draws at half scale (down to a quarter on a heavy engine) and the release redraws in full.
This spec follows the controls: open it again, or leave it open, after changing them.
